support.reason: fixes the crash/incorrect HTTP status on malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests, and makes sense to merge before #36753
confirmed that malformed 2.0 requests return HTTP 200 with error instead of HTTP 400 when tested on master with and without whitelist, and interface_rpc.py passes
verified that malformed 2.0 requests get HTTP 200 with error, invalid batch elements without id get error with id null, valid notifications get 204, and tests pass
malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests return HTTP 200 with error as spec requires, and invalid requests without id get error replies instead of being treated as notifications, alone and in batches

On master, a malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 request makes debug builds abort and gets an HTTP 400 in release builds. With this PR it gets an HTTP 200 reply with the error, as the spec requires, and invalid requests without id get error replies instead of being treated as notifications
Does indeed bring the behavior for invalid requests closer to the JSON-RPC 2.0 spec.
